files..github/workflows/changeset.yml:
name: changeset

# Release-note gate for `phoebe-agent`. Every PR that changes published
# behaviour has to carry a changeset, because `release.yml` has nothing else to
# release from: a merge with no changeset silently ships nothing, and the change
# lands on `main` with no line in CHANGELOG.md and no version bump.
#
# The check is the Changesets CLI itself — `changeset status --since` — not a
# third-party action. It is the same tool `release.yml` consumes the changesets
# with, so "the gate passed" and "the release workflow will pick this up" cannot
# drift apart. `status` resolves the files changed since the base branch to
# packages, then fails if any changed package has no pending changeset naming
# it. This repo is a single package rooted at the repo tree, so in practice the
# rule reads: any file change needs a changeset unless it is deliberately
# exempted below.
#
# Two exemptions, both intentional:
#
#   skip-changeset label — docs-only, CI-only, or test-only PRs. Note that an
#                          *empty* changeset does not satisfy `status` (it
#                          releases no package), so the label is the only way
#                          past this gate.
#   changeset-release/*  — the "chore: version packages" PR opened by
#                          `release.yml`. It exists precisely to *consume* the
#                          pending changesets, so it has none by construction.

on:
  pull_request:
    # `labeled`/`unlabeled` are here so applying `skip-changeset` re-runs the
    # gate and turns the check green without an empty push.
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, labeled, unlabeled, ready_for_review]

# Least privilege: this gate only reads the repo. It runs on `pull_request`
# (not `pull_request_target`), so the fork code it checks out is untrusted and
# holds a read-only token — it must stay that way.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: changeset-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  changeset:
    # Both exemptions are evaluated here rather than inside a step so an exempt
    # PR reports a skipped job instead of a green one that did nothing.
    if: >-
      !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'changeset-release/') &&
      !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'skip-changeset')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # fetch-depth: 0 is what makes `--since` work: at full depth
      # actions/checkout fetches every head into `refs/remotes/origin/*`, so the
      # base branch exists locally for the diff. At the default depth of 1 only
      # the PR merge ref is fetched and `origin/<base>` would not resolve.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # Same toolchain as the ready gate: installs `vp` and the Node version
      # pinned in .node-version, and caches the pnpm store.
      - uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true

      # `changeset` is a devDependency, so it has to be installed before it can
      # be run. Nothing here needs postinstall scripts.
      - run: vp install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

      # The base ref is passed through `env:` rather than interpolated into the
      # script body — same rule the vouch workflow follows for values that come
      # off the event payload.
      - name: Require a changeset
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if vp exec changeset status --since "origin/$BASE_REF"; then
            exit 0
          fi
          cat >&2 <<'MSG'

          ── This PR changes phoebe-agent but has no changeset ──────────────

          Release notes and the version bump both come from changesets, so a
          merge without one ships nothing. Add one on your branch:

              pnpm changeset

          Pick patch / minor / major, write a one-line summary aimed at someone
          reading the CHANGELOG, and commit the generated .changeset/*.md file.

          If this PR genuinely changes nothing a consumer would notice — docs,
          CI, tests, internal refactors with no behaviour change — a maintainer
          can label it `skip-changeset` instead. Applying the label re-runs
          this check.

          See docs/releasing.md.
          ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          MSG
          exit 1
files..github/workflows/ready.yml:
name: ready

# Merge gate for `phoebe-agent`. Two jobs run in parallel on every PR (and on
# main after merge):
#
#   ready           — static checks + tests against the source tree
#                     (mirrors the cloned gate from JesusFilm/youtube-studio).
#   pack-and-smoke  — packs the CLI with `npm pack` and smoke-runs the packed
#                     artifact from a scratch project. This catches packaging
#                     bugs a source-tree test misses: missing entries in
#                     package.json `files`, wrong `bin`/`exports`, or an
#                     entry-point check that trips over the bin symlink.

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# Least privilege: this gate only reads the repo.
permissions:
  contents: read

# A new push to a branch cancels its in-flight run.
concurrency:
  group: ready-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  ready:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Installs the `vp` CLI and the Node version pinned in .node-version,
      # and caches the pnpm store across runs.
      - uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true

      # --ignore-scripts skips optional postinstalls that aren't needed for
      # check/test/build; --frozen-lockfile fails on a stale lockfile.
      - run: vp install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

      # Format + lint + type-check via vp check. `-r lint`/`typecheck`/`test`
      # recurse over every package script that defines the target — in this
      # single-package repo that's just phoebe-agent, but the pattern tracks the
      # youtube-studio gate this was cloned from. `!cancelled()` keeps subsequent
      # steps running after a failure so authors see every broken check in one
      # report. There is no build step: the engine and bootstrapper run from raw
      # `.ts` via Node 24 type-stripping, so `tsc` here is typecheck-only.
      - run: vp check

      - run: vp run -r lint
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}

      - run: vp run -r typecheck
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}

      - run: vp run -r test
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
      # The last step of the root `ready` script, and the one that keeps a broken
      # Electron main from being invisible until someone packages the companion
      # (#521 §6). Building it needs no Electron binary — `--ignore-scripts`
      # above already skips the postinstall that fetches one, and this says so a
      # second time so the step keeps working if that flag ever goes.
      - run: vp run -r build
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        env:
          ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD: "1"

  pack-and-smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true

      - run: vp install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

      # No build step: the package ships raw `.ts` and runs under Node 24
      # type-stripping. `npm pack` writes phoebe-agent-<version>.tgz into the
      # current dir and includes only what package.json `files` lists:
      # bootstrap/, src/, prompts/, templates/. If a resource the bin needs at
      # runtime isn't listed there, the smoke below fails loudly.
      - name: Pack
        id: pack
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tarball=$(npm pack --silent)
          echo "tarball=$PWD/$tarball" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Install into a scratch project the CI runner owns — no source tree in
      # the resolver path, so we exercise the packed artifact the same way a
      # consumer running `npm i phoebe-agent` would.
      - name: Install packed tarball into scratch project
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p smoke && cd smoke
          npm init -y >/dev/null
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund "${{ steps.pack.outputs.tarball }}"

      # Both bin aliases point at the same script; assert both resolve and the
      # help text prints. `--no-install` refuses to reach for the registry —
      # if the local install didn't land the bin, npx would silently fetch it.
      - name: phoebe --help
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/smoke
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npx --no-install phoebe --help | tee help.out
          grep -q "phoebe — software factory for GitHub repositories" help.out

      - name: phoebe-agent --help
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/smoke
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npx --no-install phoebe-agent --help | tee help.out
          grep -q "phoebe — software factory for GitHub repositories" help.out

      # Exercise the scaffolder against the packed artifact: it reads templates/
      # and prompts/ out of the installed package, so a missing `files` entry
      # or a broken resource walk-up would blow up here.
      - name: phoebe init scaffold
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/smoke
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npx --no-install phoebe init scaffold
          test -f scaffold/phoebe.config.ts
          test -f scaffold/.env.example
          test -f scaffold/prompts/issues-prompt.md
          test -f scaffold/prompts/checks-prompt.md
          test -f scaffold/prompts/conflict-prompt.md
          test -f scaffold/prompts/reviews-prompt.md
          test -f scaffold/prompts/research-prompt.md
          test -f scaffold/container/Dockerfile
          test -f scaffold/container/compose.yml
          test -f scaffold/container/compose.local.yml
          # The two invariants that break a consumer silently rather than
          # loudly, asserted here against the *packed* templates as well as in
          # src/init.test.ts against the repo's: `phoebe boot` is the whole
          # ENTRYPOINT, and the config imports nothing at runtime.
          grep -q 'ENTRYPOINT \["/usr/bin/tini", "--", "phoebe", "boot"\]' scaffold/container/Dockerfile
          ! grep -qP '^import (?!type )' scaffold/phoebe.config.ts
files..github/workflows/release.yml:
name: release

# Release automation for `phoebe-agent`, driven by Changesets and published to
# npm with trusted publishing (OIDC) — no long-lived NPM_TOKEN.
#
# The flow, on every push to main:
#
#   1. If unreleased changesets exist under .changeset/, changesets/action opens
#      (or updates) a "Version Packages" PR that consumes them: it bumps the
#      version in package.json and writes CHANGELOG.md. Merging that PR is the
#      human release trigger.
#   2. When main already has no pending changesets (i.e. the Version Packages PR
#      just merged), the same action runs the `release` script, which runs
#      `changeset publish` — publishing any package whose version isn't yet on
#      the registry and pushing the matching git tag. There is no build: the
#      package ships raw `.ts` and runs under Node 24 type-stripping.
#   3. If that published, the `package` job builds the companion on three
#      runners and attaches the artifacts to the GitHub Release at the same
#      `phoebe-agent@x.y.z` tag (#525 §1). That release is the feed the
#      installed companion updates from (apps/desktop/src/update-feed.ts).
#
# npm trusted publishing must be configured once on npmjs.com for the
# `phoebe-agent` package, pointing at this repo and this workflow file
# (`release.yml`). See docs/releasing.md for that one-time setup.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# Serialize release runs on main: a push that lands mid-release queues behind
# the in-flight run rather than cancelling it. Never `cancel-in-progress: true`
# here — interrupting a `changeset publish` risks a half-done release (a git tag
# pushed without the matching npm publish, or vice versa).
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # push the version bump / CHANGELOG commit + git tags
  pull-requests: write # open and update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # mint the OIDC token npm exchanges for trusted publishing

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # What the packaging job needs to know: whether anything was published, and
    # at which version. The version is read off package.json after the publish
    # rather than parsed out of the action's JSON, because the tag step below
    # already reads it that way and the two must agree.
    outputs:
      published: ${{ steps.changesets.outputs.published }}
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      # Full history so changesets can read tags and compute changelogs.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # Same toolchain the ready gate uses: installs `vp` and the Node version
      # pinned in .node-version, and caches the pnpm store.
      - uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true

      - run: vp install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

      # Trusted publishing (OIDC + automatic provenance) requires npm >= 11.5.1.
      # Node 24 already bundles npm 11, but pin it explicitly so a base-image npm
      # bump can't silently move the binary the `changeset publish` step shells
      # out to. Changesets always publishes via `npm publish` (not `pnpm
      # publish`), so this is the binary that matters — and it sidesteps the pnpm
      # 11.x OIDC regression (pnpm/pnpm#11513). npm 11 already includes trusted
      # publishing, so there's no reason to jump to @latest.
      - name: Upgrade npm for trusted publishing
        run: npm install -g npm@11

      - name: Create Version Packages PR or publish
        id: changesets
        uses: changesets/action@v2.1.2
        with:
          version-script: vp run version-packages
          publish-script: vp run release
          commit-message: "chore: version packages"
          pr-title: "chore: version packages"
        env:
          # Only the GitHub token is needed. Publish auth comes from the OIDC
          # token minted via `id-token: write` above — no NPM_TOKEN.
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # changesets names its tag after the package once a repo is a workspace:
      # `phoebe-agent@x.y.z`. The engine's own `upgrade` finds releases by the
      # `vX.Y.Z` tags this repo carried before it had a workspace, on every
      # deployment already in the field (src/upgrade.ts, RELEASE_TAG), so a
      # release with only the first tag is invisible to it. Each release gets
      # both. The GitHub Release stays on the changesets tag, where the desktop
      # update feed downloads from (apps/desktop/src/update-feed.ts).
      - name: Name the version that was published
        id: version
        if: steps.changesets.outputs.published == 'true'
        run: echo "version=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Push the vX.Y.Z tag the engine's upgrade looks for
        if: steps.changesets.outputs.published == 'true'
        run: |
          tag="v${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}"
          if git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/${tag}" >/dev/null; then
            echo "${tag} is already on origin"
            exit 0
          fi
          git tag -a "${tag}" -m "${tag}"
          git push origin "${tag}"

  # The companion, packaged (#525 §1). One job per platform because each target
  # can only be built on its own OS, and `fail-fast: false` because a Windows
  # runner having a bad morning is no reason to withhold the macOS build.
  #
  # Everything here is unsigned this effort (#525 §2): no certificate, no
  # notarisation, no secret beyond the GitHub token that uploads. When the
  # signing task lands it adds credentials to this job and flips the macOS
  # clause in the companion's updater; nothing else moves.
  package:
    needs: release
    if: needs.release.outputs.published == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # Only the upload needs the token, and only to write release assets. The
    # workflow-level grant also carries pull-requests and id-token for the
    # release job; neither has any business on a runner executing a build.
    permissions:
      contents: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: macos-latest
            artifacts: release/*.dmg release/*.zip release/latest-mac.yml release/*.blockmap
          - os: windows-latest
            artifacts: release/*.exe release/latest.yml release/*.blockmap
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            artifacts: release/*.AppImage release/latest-linux.yml
    steps:
      # Nothing in this job runs git against the remote; the upload authenticates
      # through GH_TOKEN below, so the checkout keeps no credential behind.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true

      # Install scripts run here, unlike in every other job: Electron's
      # postinstall fetches the platform binary electron-builder packages the app
      # around, and `allowBuilds` in pnpm-workspace.yaml names it as the one
      # dependency allowed to do that.
      - run: vp install --frozen-lockfile

      # The console bundle and the companion's main and preload. Packaging copies
      # both out of the tree it builds them into; it does not build them itself.
      - run: vp run -r build

      - name: Package the companion
        working-directory: apps/desktop
        run: vp run package

      # Onto the release `changeset publish` tagged, rather than a release of the
      # app's own: one tag, one version, both halves of a release under it.
      # Every pattern has to match something: a manifest without its installer
      # is a release that looks complete and updates nothing, so a target that
      # silently produced less than the row lists fails the job here.
      - name: Attach the artifacts to the release
        working-directory: apps/desktop
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          files=()
          for pattern in ${{ matrix.artifacts }}; do
            if ! compgen -G "$pattern" > /dev/null; then
              echo "electron-builder produced no file matching: $pattern" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            while IFS= read -r match; do files+=("$match"); done < <(compgen -G "$pattern")
          done
          gh release upload "phoebe-agent@${{ needs.release.outputs.version }}" "${files[@]}" --clobber
